Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\cook # Cook - Smart Feature Implementation End-to-end implementation with automatic workflow detection. **Principles:** YAGNI, KISS, DRY | Token efficiency | Concise reports ## Usage ``` /ck:cook ``` **IMPORTANT:** If no flag is provided, the skill will use the `interactive` mode by default for the workflow. **Optional flags to select the workflow mode:** - `--interactive`: Full workflow with user input (**default**) - `--fast`: Skip research, scout→plan→code - `--parallel`: Multi-agent execution - `--no-test`: Skip testing step - `--auto`: Auto-approve all steps **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): - `--tdd`: Tests-first per phase — write tests for current behavior before refactoring, then verify they still pass after the implementation step **Example:** ``` /ck:cook "Add user authentication to the app" --fast /ck:cook path/to/plan.md --auto /ck:cook "Refactor auth middleware" --tdd ``` Do NOT write implementation code until a plan exists and has been reviewed. This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: plans/260517-stage2-universal-audit-completion-engine

Use these commands instead of hand-editing CLI-managed plan structure: ```bash ck plan create \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill ck plan create \ --global \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check --start cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan uncheck ck plan status /absolute/path/to/plan.md ck config ui --port 3456 ``` Rules: - Use `ck plan create` to scaffold `plan.md` and `phase-*.md` when the CLI is available. - Default scope is project-local (`./plans/` under the current project). - Global scope is conditional: use `ck plan create --global ...` or fall back to global scope only when no project context exists. - Use `ck plan check` / `ck plan uncheck` for phase status changes. - Do not hand-edit the phases table for status toggles or structural updates when CLI commands are available. - Use the dashboard at `http://localhost:3456/plans` for visual plan management. - **Overwriting phase stub files:** `ck plan create` scaffolds small boilerplate `phase-XX-*.md` stubs. Always **Read the stub before Write** — Claude Code enforces Read-before-Write on existing files; skipping the Read causes the Write to be rejected, wasting the Write's input tokens AND forcing a retry. The stubs are tiny (~15 lines), so the Read cost is trivial. Then Write the full content following the canonical template below. ### Canonical Phase File Template Use this structure when filling each `phase-XX-*.md`. Loaded once with the skill — no per-file Read needed to learn it. Frontmatter fields match the CLI's phase schema; section headers match `documentation-management.md` so phase files stay consistent across plans. ````markdown --- phase: title: "" status: pending # pending | in-progress | completed priority: P2 # P1 | P2 | P3 effort: "" # e.g. "4h", "2d" dependencies: [] # phase IDs this blocks on --- # Phase : ## Overview <1-2 sentences describing what this phase delivers> ## Requirements - Functional: ... - Non-functional: ... ## Architecture ## Related Code Files - Create: `path/...` - Modify: `path/...` - Delete: `path/...` ## Implementation Steps 1. ... 2. ... ## Success Criteria - [ ] ... ## Risk Assessment ```` **IMPORTANT:** Before you start, scan unfinished plans in the active scope first: - Project scope: `./plans/` - Global scope: the configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` If there are relevant plans overlapping your upcoming plan, update them as well. If you're unsure or need more clarifications, use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask the user. ### Scope Selection - **Project scope** is the default whenever the current working tree has project context. - **Global scope** is allowed only when: - the user explicitly asks for it via `--global`, or - there is no project context to anchor a local plan. - **No project context** means no `.git`, `package.json`, or `CLAUDE.md` was found in the ancestor chain. - Keep scope honest in prose and examples: the skill describes CLI-owned behavior, it does not implement scope resolution itself. ### Cross-Plan Dependency Detection During the pre-creation scan, detect and mark blocking relationships between plans: 1. **Scan** — Read `plan.md` frontmatter of each unfinished plan (status != `completed`/`cancelled`) 2. **Compare scope** — Check overlapping files, shared dependencies, same feature area 3. **Classify relationship:** - New plan needs output of existing plan → new plan `blockedBy: [existing-plan-dir]` - New plan changes something existing plan depends on → existing plan `blockedBy: [new-plan-dir]`, new plan `blocks: [existing-plan-dir]` - Cross-scope dependency → use `global:` or `project:` prefixes - Mutual dependency → both plans reference each other in `blockedBy`/`blocks` 4. **Bidirectional update** — When relationship detected, update BOTH `plan.md` files' frontmatter 5. **Ambiguous?** → Use `AskUserQuestion` with header "Plan Dependency", present detected overlap, ask user to confirm relationship type (blocks/blockedBy/none) **Frontmatter fields**: ```yaml blockedBy: [260301-1200-auth-system] # Same-scope dependency blockedBy: [global:260301-1200-auth-system] # Cross-scope dependency blocks: [project:260228-0900-user-dashboard] # Explicit project-scope dependency ``` **Status interaction:** `ck plan status` is the authoritative inspection surface. Load: `references/verification-roles.md` → "Whole-Plan Consistency Sweep". Before recommending `/ck:cook`, re-read `plan.md` and every `phase-*.md` file. Do not recommend cook until the whole-plan consistency sweep reports zero unresolved contradictions. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the outputs. - DO NOT implement code - only create plans - Respond with plan file path and summary - Ensure self-contained plans with necessary context - Include code snippets/pseudocode when clarifying - Fully respect the `./docs/development-rules.md` file ## Task Management Plan files = persistent. Skip with `--no-tasks`. **3-Task Rule:** <3 phases → skip task creation. **Fallback:** Task tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList`) are CLI-only — unavailable in VSCode extension. TaskCreate per phase with `addBlockedBy` chain (skip if Task tools unavailable) 3. TaskCreate for critical/high-risk steps within phases (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Cook picks up via TaskList (same session) or re-hydrates (new session) ## Active Plan State Check `## Plan Context` injected by hooks: - **"Plan: {path}"** → Active plan. Ask "Continue? [Y/n]" - **"Suggested: {path}"** → Branch hint only. Ask if activate or create new. - **"Plan: none"** → Create new using `Plan dir:` from `## Naming` After creating plan: `node .claude/scripts/set-active-plan.cjs {plan-dir}` Reports: Active plans → plan-specific path. Suggested → default path. ### Important **DO NOT** create plans or reports in arbitrary user directories. **MUST** create plans or reports in one of these allowed roots: - project scope → current working project directory - global scope → configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` ## Subcommands | Subcommand | Reference | Purpose | |------------|-----------|---------| | `/ck:plan archive` | `references/archive-workflow.md` | Archive plans + write journal entries | | `/ck:plan red-team` | `references/red-team-workflow.md` | Adversarial plan review with hostile reviewers | | `/ck:plan validate` | `references/validate-workflow.md` | Validate plan with critical questions interview | ## Post-Plan Handoff (MANDATORY at session end) After `plan.md` + phase files are written and the user has reviewed/approved them, use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate next step. 1	# Stage 2: Universal Audit-Completion Engine
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-05-17
4	**Type:** System Architecture Redesign
5	**Status:** Approved — ready for plan
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Problem Statement
10	
11	Current system produces outputs (stage0, brainstorm, think, etc.) that vary in quality 6-9/10. Quality gaps include:
12	- Missing failure archaeology
13	- Unsourced numeric claims
14	- Surface-level analysis without mechanisms
15	- Contradictions between agents
16	- Incomplete coverage of required dimensions
17	
18	Existing hooks (stage0-post-audit.cjs, research-output-validator.cjs) only BLOCK bad output. They don't DRIVE completion. User manually spots gaps and re-asks — wasting cycles.
19	
20	### Root Cause
21	System designed as single-pass pipeline: produce → validate → pass/fail. No iterative refinement loop built into the core.
22	
23	### AEVO Insight
24	Self-evolution works when feedback cycles are SHORT and VOLUME is high. Current system has long cycles (weeks for outcomes). Stage 2 creates a SHORT cycle (seconds — within same session) by auditing and re-running immediately.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Design
29	
30	### Core Concept
31	
32	Stage 2 = **always-on post-command hook** that:
33	1. Audits EVERY assistant output against type-specific quality schema
34	2. If gaps found → BLOCKS output (exit 2) with structured gap injection
35	3. Claude sees gaps → self-fixes → re-outputs → hook re-fires
36	4. Loop until 0 critical/major gaps OR convergence limit hit
37	
38	### Architecture
39	
40	```
41	ANY COMMAND OUTPUT
42	         │
43	         ▼
44	┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
45	│ stage2-audit-completion.cjs (Stop)   │
46	│                                      │
47	│ 1. Detect output type (stage0/brain/ │
48	│    brainstorm/code/plan/etc)         │
49	│ 2. Load matching audit schema        │
50	│ 3. Run D1-D7 dimension checks       │
51	│ 4. Classify gaps (critical/major/    │
52	│    minor)                            │
53	│ 5. Check convergence (anti-loop)     │
54	│ 6. If actionable gaps > 0:          │
55	│    → exit 2 + inject gap list       │
56	│    → Claude auto-retries            │
57	│ 7. If 0 actionable gaps:            │
58	│    → exit 0 (PASS)                  │
59	└──────────────────────────────────────┘
60	```
61	
62	### File Structure
63	
64	```
65	.claude/hooks/
66	├── stage2-audit-completion.cjs          # Main Stop hook
67	├── lib/
68	│   ├── audit-engine.cjs                 # Core: type detection + schema loading + gap extraction
69	│   ├── gap-classifier.cjs              # Severity scoring (critical/major/minor)
70	│   ├── convergence-detector.cjs        # Anti-infinite-loop (stagnation + repeat detection)
71	│   ├── audit-history.cjs               # Track iterations within session
72	│   └── audit-schemas/
73	│       ├── stage0.json                 # /stage0 audit criteria
74	│       ├── brainstorm.json             # /brainstorm audit criteria
75	│       ├── think.json                  # /think audit criteria
76	│       ├── code-impl.json             # Code implementation audit
77	│       ├── plan.json                   # /plan output audit
78	│       ├── invest.json                 # /invest analysis audit
79	│       ├── coffee.json                 # /coffee export audit
80	│       └── default.json               # Fallback (minimal checks)
81	```
82	
83	### Audit Dimensions (D1-D7)
84	
85	| Dim | Name | What it checks | Applies to |
86	|-----|------|----------------|-----------|
87	| D1 | Completeness | Missing required sections, skipped agents, empty dimensions | All |
88	| D2 | Consistency | Contradictions between claims, agent disagreements | All |
89	| D3 | Depth | Surface inference vs substantive analysis, mechanism explanation | Business |
90	| D4 | Evidence | Claims without [K]/[T]/[?] tags, unsourced numbers, confabulation | Business |
91	| D5 | Logic | Broken causal chains, non-sequiturs, unsupported conclusions | All |
92	| D6 | Actionability | Vague recommendations vs specific next-steps | All |
93	| D7 | Domain-specific | Per-schema custom rules (see individual schemas) | Per-type |
94	
95	### Gap Classification
96	
97	```
98	CRITICAL (must fix, auto-fixable):
99	  - Missing failure archaeology (fix: run WebSearch)
100	  - Unsourced revenue claim (fix: add [?] tag or find source)
101	  - 0 agents fired in a wave (fix: re-run wave)
102	
103	MAJOR (must fix, may need user):
104	  - Contradictions between agent outputs (fix: reconcile)
105	  - Missing competitor analysis (fix: re-research)
106	  - Confidence score without justification (fix: explain)
107	
108	MINOR (tag [RESIDUAL], don't block):
109	  - Formatting issues
110	  - Slightly surface-level in non-critical section
111	  - Missing optional section
112	```
113	
114	### Hybrid Execution Model
115	
116	```
117	Gap fix_cost determination:
118	  - "auto" (<30s): re-search, add tag, rephrase claim → hook injects instruction, LLM self-fixes
119	  - "medium" (30s-2min): re-run specific agent, deeper research → inject instruction with notice
120	  - "large" (>2min): full wave re-run, major restructure → ask user permission
121	```
122	
123	Since this is a Stop hook (cannot directly ask user), all gaps are injected as instructions. The "large" gaps include explicit text: "USER DECISION NEEDED: [description]. Say 'skip [gap-id]' to accept as-is, or address it."
124	
125	### Convergence Safety
126	
127	| Rule | Condition | Action |
128	|------|-----------|--------|
129	| Stagnation | gaps[n] >= gaps[n-1] for 2 consecutive | Force-pass with [STAGNATING] |
130	| Repeat | Same gap_id in 2+ iterations | Mark [UNFILLABLE], exclude |
131	| Max iterations | 5 iterations reached | Force-pass with [MAX_ITER] |
132	| Only minors | 0 critical + 0 major remain | Auto-pass, tag minors |
133	
134	### Integration with Existing System
135	
136	Stage 2 does NOT replace existing hooks. Execution order:
137	1. `research-output-validator.cjs` (SubagentStop — catches agent-level issues)
138	2. `stage0-post-audit.cjs` (Stop — stage0-specific presence checks)
139	3. `stage2-audit-completion.cjs` (Stop — universal quality + completion)
140	
141	Stage 2 runs LAST. If earlier hooks block first, Stage 2 never fires for that iteration.
142	
143	### Schema Example: brainstorm.json
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "type": "brainstorm",
148	  "trigger_patterns": ["brainstorm", "## Problem", "## Approach", "design doc"],
149	  "dimensions": {
150	    "completeness": {
151	      "weight": 0.3,
152	      "checks": [
153	        {"id": "problem_stated", "rule": "section_exists('problem|issue|challenge')"},
154	        {"id": "multiple_approaches", "rule": "count_pattern('approach|option|alternative') >= 2"},
155	        {"id": "tradeoffs", "rule": "contains('pro|con|tradeoff|trade-off|risk')"},
156	        {"id": "recommendation", "rule": "contains('recommend|propose|suggest')"}
157	      ]
158	    },
159	    "depth": {
160	      "weight": 0.3,
161	      "checks": [
162	        {"id": "mechanism_not_narrative", "rule": "contains('because|mechanism|caused by|works by')"},
163	        {"id": "money_flow", "rule": "contains('revenue|cost|margin|pricing|$ ') OR not_business_topic()"},
164	        {"id": "not_table_only", "rule": "prose_ratio() >= 0.4"}
165	      ]
166	    },
167	    "evidence": {
168	      "weight": 0.2,
169	      "checks": [
170	        {"id": "no_unsourced_claims", "rule": "unsourced_number_count() <= 2"},
171	        {"id": "anti_confirmation", "rule": "contains('fail|risk|concern|against') OR not_product_analysis()"}
172	      ]
173	    },
174	    "actionability": {
175	      "weight": 0.2,
176	      "checks": [
177	        {"id": "specific_next_steps", "rule": "contains('next step|TODO|action item|will')"},
178	        {"id": "concrete_not_vague", "rule": "vague_phrase_count('consider|perhaps|might want') <= 3"}
179	      ]
180	    }
181	  },
182	  "pass_criteria": {"critical": 0, "major": 0},
183	  "max_iterations": 3
184	}
185	```
186	
187	---
188	
189	## Relationship: System 1 ↔ System 2
190	
191	```
192	System 1 (Stage0, brainstorm, think, etc.)
193	    │ produces output
194	    ▼
195	System 2 (Audit hook)
196	    │ finds gaps
197	    ▼
198	System 1 (same LLM, same session)
199	    │ fills gaps based on injection
200	    ▼
201	System 2 (re-audit)
202	    │ ...loop...
203	    ▼
204	FINAL OUTPUT (quality-assured)
205	```
206	
207	Key relationship properties:

# Stage 2: Universal Audit-Completion Engine

**Date:** 2026-05-17
**Type:** System Architecture Redesign
**Status:** Approved — ready for plan

---

## Problem Statement

Current system produces outputs (stage0, brainstorm, think, etc.) that vary in quality 6-9/10. Quality gaps include:
- Missing failure archaeology
- Unsourced numeric claims
- Surface-level analysis without mechanisms
- Contradictions between agents
- Incomplete coverage of required dimensions

Existing hooks (stage0-post-audit.cjs, research-output-validator.cjs) only BLOCK bad output. They don't DRIVE completion. User manually spots gaps and re-asks — wasting cycles.

### Root Cause
System designed as single-pass pipeline: produce → validate → pass/fail. No iterative refinement loop built into the core.

### AEVO Insight
Self-evolution works when feedback cycles are SHORT and VOLUME is high. Current system has long cycles (weeks for outcomes). Stage 2 creates a SHORT cycle (seconds — within same session) by auditing and re-running immediately.

---

## Design

### Core Concept

Stage 2 = **always-on post-command hook** that:
1. Audits EVERY assistant output against type-specific quality schema
2. If gaps found → BLOCKS output (exit 2) with structured gap injection
3. Claude sees gaps → self-fixes → re-outputs → hook re-fires
4. Loop until 0 critical/major gaps OR convergence limit hit

### Architecture

```
ANY COMMAND OUTPUT
         │
         ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ stage2-audit-completion.cjs (Stop)   │
│                                      │
│ 1. Detect output type (stage0/brain/ │
│    brainstorm/code/plan/etc)         │
│ 2. Load matching audit schema        │
│ 3. Run D1-D7 dimension checks       │
│ 4. Classify gaps (critical/major/    │
│    minor)                            │
│ 5. Check convergence (anti-loop)     │
│ 6. If actionable gaps > 0:          │
│    → exit 2 + inject gap list       │
│    → Claude auto-retries            │
│ 7. If 0 actionable gaps:            │
│    → exit 0 (PASS)                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### File Structure

```
.claude/hooks/
├── stage2-audit-completion.cjs          # Main Stop hook
├── lib/
│   ├── audit-engine.cjs                 # Core: type detection + schema loading + gap extraction
│   ├── gap-classifier.cjs              # Severity scoring (critical/major/minor)
│   ├── convergence-detector.cjs        # Anti-infinite-loop (stagnation + repeat detection)
│   ├── audit-history.cjs               # Track iterations within session
│   └── audit-schemas/
│       ├── stage0.json                 # /stage0 audit criteria
│       ├── brainstorm.json             # /brainstorm audit criteria
│       ├── think.json                  # /think audit criteria
│       ├── code-impl.json             # Code implementation audit
│       ├── plan.json                   # /plan output audit
│       ├── invest.json                 # /invest analysis audit
│       ├── coffee.json                 # /coffee export audit
│       └── default.json               # Fallback (minimal checks)
```

### Audit Dimensions (D1-D7)

| Dim | Name | What it checks | Applies to |
|-----|------|----------------|-----------|
| D1 | Completeness | Missing required sections, skipped agents, empty dimensions | All |
| D2 | Consistency | Contradictions between claims, agent disagreements | All |
| D3 | Depth | Surface inference vs substantive analysis, mechanism explanation | Business |
| D4 | Evidence | Claims without [K]/[T]/[?] tags, unsourced numbers, confabulation | Business |
| D5 | Logic | Broken causal chains, non-sequiturs, unsupported conclusions | All |
| D6 | Actionability | Vague recommendations vs specific next-steps | All |
| D7 | Domain-specific | Per-schema custom rules (see individual schemas) | Per-type |

### Gap Classification

```
CRITICAL (must fix, auto-fixable):
  - Missing failure archaeology (fix: run WebSearch)
  - Unsourced revenue claim (fix: add [?] tag or find source)
  - 0 agents fired in a wave (fix: re-run wave)

MAJOR (must fix, may need user):
  - Contradictions between agent outputs (fix: reconcile)
  - Missing competitor analysis (fix: re-research)
  - Confidence score without justification (fix: explain)

MINOR (tag [RESIDUAL], don't block):
  - Formatting issues
  - Slightly surface-level in non-critical section
  - Missing optional section
```

### Hybrid Execution Model

```
Gap fix_cost determination:
  - "auto" (<30s): re-search, add tag, rephrase claim → hook injects instruction, LLM self-fixes
  - "medium" (30s-2min): re-run specific agent, deeper research → inject instruction with notice
  - "large" (>2min): full wave re-run, major restructure → ask user permission
```

Since this is a Stop hook (cannot directly ask user), all gaps are injected as instructions. The "large" gaps include explicit text: "USER DECISION NEEDED: [description]. Say 'skip [gap-id]' to accept as-is, or address it."

### Convergence Safety

| Rule | Condition | Action |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Stagnation | gaps[n] >= gaps[n-1] for 2 consecutive | Force-pass with [STAGNATING] |
| Repeat | Same gap_id in 2+ iterations | Mark [UNFILLABLE], exclude |
| Max iterations | 5 iterations reached | Force-pass with [MAX_ITER] |
| Only minors | 0 critical + 0 major remain | Auto-pass, tag minors |

### Integration with Existing System

Stage 2 does NOT replace existing hooks. Execution order:
1. `research-output-validator.cjs` (SubagentStop — catches agent-level issues)
2. `stage0-post-audit.cjs` (Stop — stage0-specific presence checks)
3. `stage2-audit-completion.cjs` (Stop — universal quality + completion)

Stage 2 runs LAST. If earlier hooks block first, Stage 2 never fires for that iteration.

### Schema Example: brainstorm.json

```json
{
  "type": "brainstorm",
  "trigger_patterns": ["brainstorm", "## Problem", "## Approach", "design doc"],
  "dimensions": {
    "completeness": {
      "weight": 0.3,
      "checks": [
        {"id": "problem_stated", "rule": "section_exists('problem|issue|challenge')"},
        {"id": "multiple_approaches", "rule": "count_pattern('approach|option|alternative') >= 2"},
        {"id": "tradeoffs", "rule": "contains('pro|con|tradeoff|trade-off|risk')"},
        {"id": "recommendation", "rule": "contains('recommend|propose|suggest')"}
      ]
    },
    "depth": {
      "weight": 0.3,
      "checks": [
        {"id": "mechanism_not_narrative", "rule": "contains('because|mechanism|caused by|works by')"},
        {"id": "money_flow", "rule": "contains('revenue|cost|margin|pricing|$ ') OR not_business_topic()"},
        {"id": "not_table_only", "rule": "prose_ratio() >= 0.4"}
      ]
    },
    "evidence": {
      "weight": 0.2,
      "checks": [
        {"id": "no_unsourced_claims", "rule": "unsourced_number_count() <= 2"},
        {"id": "anti_confirmation", "rule": "contains('fail|risk|concern|against') OR not_product_analysis()"}
      ]
    },
    "actionability": {
      "weight": 0.2,
      "checks": [
        {"id": "specific_next_steps", "rule": "contains('next step|TODO|action item|will')"},
        {"id": "concrete_not_vague", "rule": "vague_phrase_count('consider|perhaps|might want') <= 3"}
      ]
    }
  },
  "pass_criteria": {"critical": 0, "major": 0},
  "max_iterations": 3
}
```

---

## Relationship: System 1 ↔ System 2

```
System 1 (Stage0, brainstorm, think, etc.)
    │ produces output
    ▼
System 2 (Audit hook)
    │ finds gaps
    ▼
System 1 (same LLM, same session)
    │ fills gaps based on injection
    ▼
System 2 (re-audit)
    │ ...loop...
    ▼
FINAL OUTPUT (quality-assured)
```

Key relationship properties:
- **Tight coupling**: System 2 KNOWS System 1's internals (schemas match command specs)
- **Unidirectional control**: System 2 drives System 1, never reverse
- **Same session**: No cross-session state needed (audit history is per-session)
- **Complementary**: System 1 produces, System 2 ensures quality. Neither replaces the other.
- **Progressive**: System 2 schemas can be tightened over time as System 1 improves

---

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Before | Target |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Average output quality (manual score) | 6-7/10 | 8.5+/10 |
| Gaps found post-delivery by user | 3-5 per output | <1 per output |
| Stage0 agent coverage | Often <8 (hook blocks) | Always 8+ (auto-fixed) |
| Unsourced claims in final output | 5-10 per analysis | 0-2 (all tagged [?]) |
| User re-ask rate ("but what about X?") | High | Near-zero |

---

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|-----------|
| Infinite loop (gap never fills) | High | Convergence detector: stagnation + max_iter |
| False positives (valid output blocked) | Medium | Start with conservative schemas, tighten iteratively |
| Token waste (unnecessary iterations) | Medium | Minor gaps don't block; only critical/major trigger loop |
| Hook performance (slow audit) | Low | All checks are regex/string ops, no LLM calls in hook |
| Schema maintenance burden | Low | Start with 3 schemas (stage0, brainstorm, default), add as needed |

---

## Implementation Approach

Phase 1: Core engine + default schema (works on all outputs)
Phase 2: stage0-specific schema (replace existing stage0-post-audit behavior)
Phase 3: brainstorm + think schemas
Phase 4: code + plan schemas
Phase 5: Convergence tuning from real usage data

---

## Non-Goals (Out of Scope)

- Does NOT replace existing evolution system (meta-evolution, strategy evolution)
- Does NOT generate new content — only audits and requests completion
- Does NOT cross sessions — audit state is per-session only
- Does NOT require new Python infrastructure — pure JS/CJS in hooks
- Does NOT slow down simple queries (quick detection: if output < 500 chars → skip audit)

# Stage 2: Universal Audit-Completion Engine

## Overview

A `Stop` hook (`stage2-audit-completion.cjs`) that fires after every assistant turn, detects output type, loads matching audit schema, runs D1-D7 dimension checks, and either passes (exit 0) or blocks with structured gap injection (exit 2) to drive self-correction loops. Convergence safety prevents infinite loops.

**Source:** `plans/reports/brainstorm-260517-stage2-universal-audit-completion-engine.md`

## Key Decisions

- Pure CJS (no Python, no LLM calls in hook) — regex/string ops only
- Per-session audit history (no cross-session state)
- Only critical/major gaps block; minors tagged [RESIDUAL] and passed
- Convergence: max 5 iterations, stagnation detection, repeat gap marking
- Runs LAST after existing hooks (research-output-validator, stage0-post-audit)

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort |
|-------|------|--------|--------|
| 1 | [Core Engine + Default Schema](./phase-01-core-engine-default-schema.md) | Pending | 4h |
| 2 | [Stage0 Schema + Integration](./phase-02-stage0-schema-integration.md) | Pending | 3h |
| 3 | [Brainstorm + Think Schemas](./phase-03-brainstorm-think-schemas.md) | Pending | 2h |
| 4 | [Code + Plan Schemas](./phase-04-code-plan-schemas.md) | Pending | 2h |
| 5 | [Convergence Tuning + Settings Hook](./phase-05-convergence-tuning-settings-hook.md) | Pending | 2h |

## Dependencies

- Existing `research-output-validator.cjs` and `stage0-post-audit.cjs` hooks (must not conflict)
- Hook lib utilities: `ck-config-utils.cjs`, `hook-logger.cjs`
- `settings.json` Stop hook slot (currently empty — no conflicts)

# Phase 1: Core Engine + Default Schema

## Overview

Build the main Stop hook entry point, audit engine library, gap classifier, convergence detector, audit history tracker, and a minimal default schema that works on all output types.

## Requirements

- Functional: Hook fires on every assistant turn, detects output type, loads schema, runs checks, blocks/passes
- Non-functional: <100ms execution (regex only, no LLM calls), no crashes on malformed input

## Architecture

```
stage2-audit-completion.cjs (Stop hook entry)
  → lib/audit-engine.cjs (type detection + schema load + check runner)
  → lib/gap-classifier.cjs (severity scoring)
  → lib/convergence-detector.cjs (stagnation/repeat/max-iter)
  → lib/audit-history.cjs (per-session iteration tracking)
  → lib/audit-schemas/default.json (fallback schema)
```

**Data flow:**
1. Hook receives `assistant_response` from stdin (Claude Code Stop hook protocol)
2. `audit-engine` detects type via trigger patterns
3. Loads matching schema (or default)
4. Runs D1-D7 checks applicable to schema
5. `gap-classifier` scores each failed check
6. `convergence-detector` checks iteration history
7. If actionable gaps + not converged → exit 2 + stderr gap injection
8. If no actionable gaps OR converged → exit 0

## Related Code Files

- Create: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-engine.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/gap-classifier.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/convergence-detector.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-history.cjs`
- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/default.json`

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `audit-history.cjs`** — In-memory Map keyed by session. Track: iteration count, gap IDs per iteration, timestamps. Export: `recordIteration(gaps)`, `getHistory()`, `getIterationCount()`.

2. **Create `convergence-detector.cjs`** — Import audit-history. Implement 4 rules:
   - Stagnation: `gaps[n].length >= gaps[n-1].length` for 2 consecutive → force-pass
   - Repeat: same gap_id appears in 2+ iterations → mark `[UNFILLABLE]`, exclude from actionable count
   - Max iterations: count >= 5 → force-pass
   - Only minors: 0 critical + 0 major → pass
   Export: `shouldPass(currentGaps)` returning `{pass: bool, reason: string, unfillable: string[]}`

3. **Create `gap-classifier.cjs`** — Given a list of failed checks (from schema), classify each:
   - `critical`: check has `severity: "critical"` in schema OR matches critical patterns (missing required section, unsourced revenue claim, 0 agents fired)
   - `major`: check has `severity: "major"` OR involves contradictions/missing competitor/unjustified scores
   - `minor`: everything else
   Export: `classifyGaps(failedChecks)` returning `{critical: [], major: [], minor: []}`

4. **Create `audit-engine.cjs`** — Core logic:
   - `detectType(text)`: match against all schema trigger_patterns, return best match or "default"
   - `loadSchema(type)`: require from `./audit-schemas/{type}.json`
   - `runChecks(text, schema)`: for each dimension's checks, evaluate rule against text. Rules are simple string ops: `section_exists(pattern)`, `contains(pattern)`, `count_pattern(pattern)`, `unsourced_number_count()`, `vague_phrase_count(phrases)`, `prose_ratio()`
   - Export: `audit(text)` returning `{type, passed, gaps: {critical, major, minor}, iteration, converged, reason}`

5. **Create `default.json` schema** — Minimal checks applicable to ALL outputs:
   - D1 completeness: output length > 200 chars (skip trivial responses)
   - D5 logic: no "TODO" or "PLACEHOLDER" remaining
   - D6 actionability: contains at least one concrete statement (not all questions)

6. **Create `stage2-audit-completion.cjs`** — Stop hook entry:
   - Read stdin (assistant response text)
   - Skip if output < 500 chars (trivial/conversational)
   - Skip if `isHookEnabled('stage2-audit-completion')` returns false
   - Call `audit(text)`
   - If passed → exit 0
   - If blocked → write gap list to stderr in structured format, exit 2
   - Gap injection format:
     ```
     [STAGE2-AUDIT] Iteration {n}/5 — {critical} critical, {major} major gaps found:
     {gap_id}: {description} — Fix: {fix_instruction}
     ...
     Address these gaps in your response. Say 'skip {gap_id}' for any you cannot fix.
     ```

7. **Write tests** — Unit tests for each module in `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/`:
   - `audit-history.test.cjs`
   - `convergence-detector.test.cjs`
   - `gap-classifier.test.cjs`
   - `audit-engine.test.cjs`

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hook loads without error on `node stage2-audit-completion.cjs` with mocked stdin
- [ ] Default schema passes trivial responses (<500 chars) without blocking
- [ ] Default schema catches "TODO" / "PLACEHOLDER" in substantive outputs
- [ ] Convergence: max 5 iterations enforced
- [ ] Convergence: stagnation detected after 2 same-or-worse iterations
- [ ] Convergence: repeat gaps marked [UNFILLABLE] and excluded
- [ ] Gap injection format renders cleanly in Claude Code feedback
- [ ] Execution time < 100ms on 5000-char input
- [ ] All unit tests pass

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| False positives on conversational replies | Skip audit for output < 500 chars |
| Hook crash breaks all sessions | Wrap entire hook in try/catch → exit 0 on error |
| Stdin parsing failure | Graceful fallback: if parse fails → exit 0 (fail-open) |

10	# Phase 2: Stage0 Schema + Integration
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	Create stage0-specific audit schema covering the 11-step pipeline's quality requirements. Integrate with existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs` to avoid duplication — Stage 2 subsumes or extends its checks.
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Functional: Catch stage0 outputs missing failure archaeology, unsourced claims, agent coverage gaps, contradictions
19	- Non-functional: Compatible with existing stage0-post-audit (either replace or complement)
20	
21	## Architecture
22	
23	Stage0 schema checks map to brainstorm D1-D7:
24	- D1 (Completeness): All required sections present (profile, waves, verdict, execution path)
25	- D2 (Consistency): No contradictions between agent verdicts
26	- D3 (Depth): Mechanism explanations, not just scores
27	- D4 (Evidence): Zone tags on claims, failure archaeology present
28	- D5 (Logic): Verdict supported by evidence, not arbitrary
29	- D6 (Actionability): Execution path has specific steps, not vague
30	- D7 (Domain): Agent coverage >= 8, wave coverage, ground-truth references
31	
32	## Related Code Files
33	
34	- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/stage0.json`
35	- Modify: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs` (if trigger pattern refinement needed)
36	- Read: `.claude/hooks/stage0-post-audit.cjs` (understand existing checks to avoid duplication)
37	
38	## Implementation Steps
39	
40	1. **Audit existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs`** — Extract all checks it performs. Map each to D1-D7 dimensions. Determine: which checks Stage 2 can absorb vs which remain in the existing hook.
41	
42	2. **Create `stage0.json` schema:**
43	   ```json
44	   {
45	     "type": "stage0",
46	     "trigger_patterns": ["/stage0", "## Stage 0", "VERDICT:", "Kill Probability"],
47	     "dimensions": {
48	       "completeness": {
49	         "weight": 0.25,
50	         "checks": [
51	           {"id": "s0_profile", "rule": "section_exists('profile|founder|constraints')", "severity": "critical"},
52	           {"id": "s0_verdict", "rule": "section_exists('verdict|recommendation|GO|KILL')", "severity": "critical"},
53	           {"id": "s0_execution", "rule": "section_exists('execution|next step|action plan')", "severity": "major"},
54	           {"id": "s0_risk", "rule": "section_exists('risk|danger|concern|threat')", "severity": "major"}
55	         ]
56	       },
57	       "evidence": {
58	         "weight": 0.25,
59	         "checks": [
60	           {"id": "s0_failure_arch", "rule": "contains('fail|bankrupt|closed|shut down|post-mortem')", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Run failure archaeology WebSearch for this business category"},
61	           {"id": "s0_zone_tags", "rule": "zone_tag_ratio() >= 0.3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Add [K]/[T]/[?] tags to all factual claims"},
62	           {"id": "s0_sourced_numbers", "rule": "unsourced_number_count() <= 3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Source or tag [?] remaining unsourced numeric claims"}
63	         ]
64	       },
65	       "depth": {
66	         "weight": 0.2,
67	         "checks": [
68	           {"id": "s0_mechanism", "rule": "contains('because|mechanism|works by|caused by|driven by')", "severity": "major"},
69	           {"id": "s0_money_flow", "rule": "contains('revenue|margin|cost|pricing|unit economics')", "severity": "major"},
70	           {"id": "s0_not_surface", "rule": "avg_paragraph_length() >= 3", "severity": "minor"}
71	         ]
72	       },
73	       "consistency": {
74	         "weight": 0.15,
75	         "checks": [
76	           {"id": "s0_no_contradiction", "rule": "no_score_contradiction()", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Reconcile contradicting agent assessments"},
77	           {"id": "s0_verdict_matches", "rule": "verdict_aligned_with_scores()", "severity": "major"}
78	         ]
79	       },
80	       "domain_specific": {
81	         "weight": 0.15,
82	         "checks": [
83	           {"id": "s0_agent_count", "rule": "count_pattern('persona|agent|analysis by') >= 8", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Fire additional agents to reach minimum 8 coverage"},
84	           {"id": "s0_anti_confirm", "rule": "contains('against|risk|fail|competition|alternative')", "severity": "major"}
85	         ]
86	       }
87	     },
88	     "pass_criteria": {"critical": 0, "major": 0},
89	     "max_iterations": 4
90	   }
91	   ```
92	
93	3. **Implement domain-specific rule functions** in `audit-engine.cjs`:
94	   - `zone_tag_ratio()`: count [K]/[T]/[?] tags vs factual sentences
95	   - `no_score_contradiction()`: detect if same entity scored both high and low
96	   - `verdict_aligned_with_scores()`: check verdict direction matches majority of sub-scores
97	   - `avg_paragraph_length()`: average sentences per paragraph
98	
99	4. **Integration decision:** If `stage0-post-audit.cjs` checks are fully absorbed by Stage 2, add comment in that hook noting Stage 2 now handles quality (but keep the hook for backward compat — disable it via `ck-config-utils` if Stage 2 is enabled).
100	
101	5. **Write tests** — `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/stage0-schema.test.cjs` with sample stage0 outputs (passing and failing).
102	
103	## Success Criteria
104	
105	- [ ] Stage0 schema triggers on `/stage0` outputs
106	- [ ] Missing failure archaeology → critical gap with fix instruction
107	- [ ] Unsourced claims > 3 → major gap
108	- [ ] Agent count < 8 → critical gap
109	- [ ] Contradictions between agents → critical gap
110	- [ ] Clean stage0 output passes without blocking
111	- [ ] No conflict with existing stage0-post-audit.cjs
112	
113	## Risk Assessment
114	
115	| Risk | Mitigation |
116	|------|-----------|

# Phase 2: Stage0 Schema + Integration

## Overview

Create stage0-specific audit schema covering the 11-step pipeline's quality requirements. Integrate with existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs` to avoid duplication — Stage 2 subsumes or extends its checks.

## Requirements

- Functional: Catch stage0 outputs missing failure archaeology, unsourced claims, agent coverage gaps, contradictions
- Non-functional: Compatible with existing stage0-post-audit (either replace or complement)

## Architecture

Stage0 schema checks map to brainstorm D1-D7:
- D1 (Completeness): All required sections present (profile, waves, verdict, execution path)
- D2 (Consistency): No contradictions between agent verdicts
- D3 (Depth): Mechanism explanations, not just scores
- D4 (Evidence): Zone tags on claims, failure archaeology present
- D5 (Logic): Verdict supported by evidence, not arbitrary
- D6 (Actionability): Execution path has specific steps, not vague
- D7 (Domain): Agent coverage >= 8, wave coverage, ground-truth references

## Related Code Files

- Create: `.claude/hooks/lib/audit-schemas/stage0.json`
- Modify: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs` (if trigger pattern refinement needed)
- Read: `.claude/hooks/stage0-post-audit.cjs` (understand existing checks to avoid duplication)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Audit existing `stage0-post-audit.cjs`** — Extract all checks it performs. Map each to D1-D7 dimensions. Determine: which checks Stage 2 can absorb vs which remain in the existing hook.

2. **Create `stage0.json` schema:**
   ```json
   {
     "type": "stage0",
     "trigger_patterns": ["/stage0", "## Stage 0", "VERDICT:", "Kill Probability"],
     "dimensions": {
       "completeness": {
         "weight": 0.25,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_profile", "rule": "section_exists('profile|founder|constraints')", "severity": "critical"},
           {"id": "s0_verdict", "rule": "section_exists('verdict|recommendation|GO|KILL')", "severity": "critical"},
           {"id": "s0_execution", "rule": "section_exists('execution|next step|action plan')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_risk", "rule": "section_exists('risk|danger|concern|threat')", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       },
       "evidence": {
         "weight": 0.25,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_failure_arch", "rule": "contains('fail|bankrupt|closed|shut down|post-mortem')", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Run failure archaeology WebSearch for this business category"},
           {"id": "s0_zone_tags", "rule": "zone_tag_ratio() >= 0.3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Add [K]/[T]/[?] tags to all factual claims"},
           {"id": "s0_sourced_numbers", "rule": "unsourced_number_count() <= 3", "severity": "major", "fix": "Source or tag [?] remaining unsourced numeric claims"}
         ]
       },
       "depth": {
         "weight": 0.2,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_mechanism", "rule": "contains('because|mechanism|works by|caused by|driven by')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_money_flow", "rule": "contains('revenue|margin|cost|pricing|unit economics')", "severity": "major"},
           {"id": "s0_not_surface", "rule": "avg_paragraph_length() >= 3", "severity": "minor"}
         ]
       },
       "consistency": {
         "weight": 0.15,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_no_contradiction", "rule": "no_score_contradiction()", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Reconcile contradicting agent assessments"},
           {"id": "s0_verdict_matches", "rule": "verdict_aligned_with_scores()", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       },
       "domain_specific": {
         "weight": 0.15,
         "checks": [
           {"id": "s0_agent_count", "rule": "count_pattern('persona|agent|analysis by') >= 8", "severity": "critical", "fix": "Fire additional agents to reach minimum 8 coverage"},
           {"id": "s0_anti_confirm", "rule": "contains('against|risk|fail|competition|alternative')", "severity": "major"}
         ]
       }
     },
     "pass_criteria": {"critical": 0, "major": 0},
     "max_iterations": 4
   }
   ```

3. **Implement domain-specific rule functions** in `audit-engine.cjs`:
   - `zone_tag_ratio()`: count [K]/[T]/[?] tags vs factual sentences
   - `no_score_contradiction()`: detect if same entity scored both high and low
   - `verdict_aligned_with_scores()`: check verdict direction matches majority of sub-scores
   - `avg_paragraph_length()`: average sentences per paragraph

4. **Integration decision:** If `stage0-post-audit.cjs` checks are fully absorbed by Stage 2, add comment in that hook noting Stage 2 now handles quality (but keep the hook for backward compat — disable it via `ck-config-utils` if Stage 2 is enabled).

5. **Write tests** — `.claude/hooks/__tests__/stage2/stage0-schema.test.cjs` with sample stage0 outputs (passing and failing).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Stage0 schema triggers on `/stage0` outputs
- [ ] Missing failure archaeology → critical gap with fix instruction
- [ ] Unsourced claims > 3 → major gap
- [ ] Agent count < 8 → critical gap
- [ ] Contradictions between agents → critical gap
- [ ] Clean stage0 output passes without blocking
- [ ] No conflict with existing stage0-post-audit.cjs

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Over-blocking stage0 (too strict) | Start with critical-only blocking, major as warnings first iteration |
| Regex fails on creative formatting | Test against 5+ real stage0 outputs from recent sessions |
| Duplicate blocking with existing hook | Explicit precedence: existing hook fires first, Stage 2 catches what it misses |

# Phase 5: Convergence Tuning + Settings Hook

## Overview

Register the hook in `settings.json`, add enable/disable toggle via `ck-config-utils`, tune convergence thresholds based on real outputs, and add observability (iteration count reporting).

## Requirements

- Functional: Hook wired in settings.json Stop event, killswitch via config, iteration metrics
- Non-functional: Zero-downtime activation (can be enabled/disabled without restart)

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `.claude/settings.json` — add Stop hook entry

- Modify: `.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs` — add metrics/logging

## Implementation Steps

1. **Register in `settings.json`:**

   "Stop": [
     {
       "matcher": "*",
       "hooks": [

           "command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/stage2-audit-completion.cjs",

That's fine.

The actual issue: the `contains` function receives `revenue') OR contains('cost` because the `boolMatch` regex `^(\w+)\((.*?)\)$` — with `$` — requires the string to end at `)`. For `contains('revenue')` alone it works. But in the OR split, each part is `contains('revenue')` and `contains('cost')` — should work. 

Wait, the error shows `contains` is being called with `revenue') OR contains('cost` — meaning the first regex match (compareMatch or boolMatch) is NOT failing, it's somehow matching. Let me check: `contains('revenue') OR contains('cost')` — the `boolMatch` regex is `/^(\w+)\((.*?)\)$/` which uses `.*?` (non-greedy) — it would match: fn=`contains`, args=`'revenue'` and the rest ` OR contains('cost')` won't match because of `$`. Actually with the `$` anchor, the whole string `contains('revenue') OR contains('cost')` must end with `)` — and it does! So `boolMatch` matches with:

Wait no — `.*?` is non-greedy, but it'll still backtrack to allow the final `)$` to match. So it matches the LAST `)`. The captured group becomes `'revenue') OR contains('cost'`.

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\brainstorm # Brainstorming Skill You are a Solution Brainstormer, an elite software engineering expert who specializes in system architecture design and technical decision-making. Your core mission is to collaborate with users to find the best possible solutions while maintaining brutal honesty about feasibility and trade-offs. ## Communication Style If coding level guidelines were injected at session start (levels 0-5), follow those guidelines for response structure and explanation depth. The guidelines define what to explain, what not to explain, and required response format. ## Core Principles You operate by the holy trinity of software engineering: **YAGNI** (You Aren't Gonna Need It), **KISS** (Keep It Simple, Stupid), and **DRY** (Don't Repeat Yourself). Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. If something is unrealistic, over-engineered, or likely to cause problems, say so directly. Your job is to prevent costly mistakes. 3. **Explore Alternatives**: Always consider multiple approaches. Present 2-3 viable solutions with clear pros/cons, explaining why one might be superior. 4. **Challenge Assumptions**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to question the user's initial approach. Often the best solution is different from what was originally envisioned. 5. **Consider All Stakeholders**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to evaluate impact on end users, developers, operations team, and business objectives. ## Collaboration Tools - Consult the `planner` agent to research industry best practices and find proven solutions - Engage the `docs-manager` agent to understand existing project implementation and constraints - Use `WebSearch` tool to find efficient approaches and learn from others' experiences - Use `ck:docs-seeker` skill to read latest documentation of external plugins/packages - Leverage `ck:ai-multimodal` skill to analyze visual materials and mockups - Query `psql` command to understand current database structure and existing data - Employ `ck:sequential-thinking` skill for complex problem-solving that requires structured analysis Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY brainstorming session regardless of perceived simplicity. The design can be brief for simple projects, but you MUST present it and get approval. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Current patterns/conventions already in use for similar features 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any related plans in `./plans/` 5. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify? If any of these is still vague after one round of questions, ask another round. Do NOT proceed to design with hand-wavy answers like "make it better", "add some validation", "improve UX". Push for concrete examples, sample inputs/outputs, or a reference to mimic. Use `AskUserQuestion` with options grounded in what scout found (e.g., "Should the new endpoint live in `src/api/users.ts` (existing pattern) or a new `src/api/profile/` module?") — never ask abstract questions when the codebase already constrains the answer. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple projects = most wasted work from unexamined assumptions. | | "I already know the solution" | Then writing it down takes 30 seconds. Do it. | | "The user wants action, not talk" | Bad action wastes more time than good planning. | | "Let me explore the code first" | Brainstorming tells you HOW to explore. Follow the process. | | "I'll just prototype quickly" | Prototypes become production code. Design first. | ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] --> A2[Summarize Findings to User] A2 --> B[Ask Clarifying Questions grounded in scout] B --> B2{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} B2 -->|No| B B2 -->|Yes| C{Scope too large?} C -->|Yes| D[Decompose into Sub-Projects] D --> B C -->|No| E[Propose 2-3 Approaches] E --> F[Present Design Sections] F --> G{User Approves?} G -->|No| F G -->|Yes| H[Write Design Doc / Report] H --> I{Create Plan?} I -->|Yes| J[Pick /ck:plan mode
--tdd or default] I -->|No| K[End Session] J --> L[Journal] K --> L ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. The terminal state is either `/ck:plan` or end. ## Your Process 1. **Scout Phase (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)**: Always run before anything else. - Use `ck:scout` skill (or Glob/Grep directly for small repos) to map files relevant to the user's topic - Read `./README.md` and any `./docs/*.md` files relevant to the area - Identify the project type, language, framework, and existing patterns/conventions - Note existing modules that the request will likely touch - List any in-flight plans in `./plans/` related to the topic - Output a brief codebase-context summary (3-6 bullets) to the user before asking questions 2. **Discovery Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to extract EXACT requirements (see HARD-GATE-EXACT-REQUIREMENTS). Ground every option in what scout found.    - **Stop hook**: Claude Code hook that fires after every assistant turn, can block (exit 2) or pass (exit 0)
   - **Audit schemas**: JSON files defining type-specific quality checks (D1-D7 dimensions)
   - **Convergence detector**: Anti-infinite-loop with stagnation, repeat gap, max-iter rules

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `D:\code\invesments\master_investments\.claude\hooks\stage2-audit-completion.cjs` — Main Stop hook entry point. Reads stdin, extracts assistant text, skips <500 chars, runs audit, blocks or passes.

   - `D:\code\invesments\master_investments\.claude\hooks\lib\audit-history.cjs` — Per-session Map tracking iterations, gap IDs, timestamps.

   - `D:\code\invesments\master_investments\.claude\hooks\lib\gap-classifier.cjs` — Classifies into critical/major/minor with fix_cost field.
   - `D:\code\invesments\master_investments\.claude\hooks\lib\audit-schemas\` — 8 JSON schemas: default, stage0, brainstorm, think, code-impl, plan, invest, coffee

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\brainstorm # Brainstorming Skill You are a Solution Brainstormer, an elite software engineering expert who specializes in system architecture design and technical decision-making. Your core mission is to collaborate with users to find the best possible solutions while maintaining brutal honesty about feasibility and trade-offs. ## Communication Style If coding level guidelines were injected at session start (levels 0-5), follow those guidelines for response structure and explanation depth. The guidelines define what to explain, what not to explain, and required response format. ## Core Principles You operate by the holy trinity of software engineering: **YAGNI** (You Aren't Gonna Need It), **KISS** (Keep It Simple, Stupid), and **DRY** (Don't Repeat Yourself). Every solution you propose must honor these principles. ## Your Expertise - System architecture design and scalability patterns - Risk assessment and mitigation strategies - Development time optimization and resource allocation - User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX) optimization - Technical debt management and maintainability - Performance optimization and bottleneck identification ## Your Approach 1. **Question Everything**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask probing questions to fully understand the user's request, constraints, and true objectives. Don't assume - clarify until you're 100% certain. 2. **Brutal Honesty**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to provide frank, unfiltered feedback about ideas. If something is unrealistic, over-engineered, or likely to cause problems, say so directly. Your job is to prevent costly mistakes. 3. **Explore Alternatives**: Always consider multiple approaches. Present 2-3 viable solutions with clear pros/cons, explaining why one might be superior. 4. **Challenge Assumptions**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to question the user's initial approach. Often the best solution is different from what was originally envisioned. 5. **Consider All Stakeholders**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to evaluate impact on end users, developers, operations team, and business objectives. ## Collaboration Tools - Consult the `planner` agent to research industry best practices and find proven solutions - Engage the `docs-manager` agent to understand existing project implementation and constraints - Use `WebSearch` tool to find efficient approaches and learn from others' experiences - Use `ck:docs-seeker` skill to read latest documentation of external plugins/packages - Leverage `ck:ai-multimodal` skill to analyze visual materials and mockups - Query `psql` command to understand current database structure and existing data - Employ `ck:sequential-thinking` skill for complex problem-solving that requires structured analysis Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY brainstorming session regardless of perceived simplicity. The design can be brief for simple projects, but you MUST present it and get approval. Before asking ANY clarifying question or proposing ANY approach, you MUST scan the codebase first. No exceptions. Mandatory scout outputs (collect before Discovery Phase): 1. Project type, primary language(s), framework(s) — from package.json/pyproject.toml/go.mod/Cargo.toml/etc. 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the user's topic (use `ck:scout` or Glob/Grep) 3. Current patterns/conventions already in use for similar features 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any related plans in `./plans/` 5. Constraints discovered (tech stack lock-in, existing schemas, public APIs, naming conventions) Why: clarifying questions asked WITHOUT codebase context produce vague answers and wasted cycles. Scout first → ask specific questions grounded in what already exists. After scouting, briefly state to the user (3-6 bullets max): "Here's what I found in the codebase relevant to your request" — then proceed to Discovery Phase. Discovery Phase questions MUST extract EXACT, CONCRETE requirements — not vague intent. Before proposing approaches, you MUST be able to answer in one sentence each: 1. **Expected output**: what artifact(s) does the user expect at the end? (file, feature behavior, UI screen, API response shape, CLI command, etc.) — be concrete enough to verify it later. 2. **Acceptance criteria**: how will the user know it's done correctly? (specific behaviors, inputs/outputs, edge cases that must work) 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope for this round? 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: tech stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will this interact with or modify? If any of these is still vague after one round of questions, ask another round. Do NOT proceed to design with hand-wavy answers like "make it better", "add some validation", "improve UX". Push for concrete examples, sample inputs/outputs, or a reference to mimic. Use `AskUserQuestion` with options grounded in what scout found (e.g., "Should the new endpoint live in `src/api/users.ts` (existing pattern) or a new `src/api/profile/` module?") — never ask abstract questions when the codebase already constrains the answer. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple projects = most wasted work from unexamined assumptions. | | "I already know the solution" | Then writing it down takes 30 seconds. Do it. | | "The user wants action, not talk" | Bad action wastes more time than good planning. | | "Let me explore the code first" | Brainstorming tells you HOW to explore. Follow the process. | | "I'll just prototype quickly" | Prototypes become production code. Design first. | ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] --> A2[Summarize Findings to User] A2 --> B[Ask Clarifying Questions grounded in scout] B --> B2{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} B2 -->|No| B B2 -->|Yes| C{Scope too large?} C -->|Yes| D[Decompose into Sub-Projects] D --> B C -->|No| E[Propose 2-3 Approaches] E --> F[Present Design Sections] F --> G{User Approves?} G -->|No| F G -->|Yes| H[Write Design Doc / Report] H --> I{Create Plan?} I -->|Yes| J[Pick /ck:plan mode
--tdd or default] I -->|No| K[End Session] J --> L[Journal] K --> L ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. The terminal state is either `/ck:plan` or end. ## Your Process 1. **Scout Phase (MANDATORY FIRST STEP)**: Always run before anything else. - Use `ck:scout` skill (or Glob/Grep directly for small repos) to map files relevant to the user's topic - Read `./README.md` and any `./docs/*.md` files relevant to the area - Identify the project type, language, framework, and existing patterns/conventions - Note existing modules that the request will likely touch - List any in-flight plans in `./plans/` related to the topic - Output a brief codebase-context summary (3-6 bullets) to the user before asking questions 2. **Discovery Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to extract EXACT requirements (see HARD-GATE-EXACT-REQUIREMENTS). Ground every option in what scout found. Loop until the 5 mandatory items (expected output, acceptance criteria, scope boundary, non-negotiable constraints, touchpoints) are concrete. 3. **Scope Assessment**: Before deep-diving, assess if request covers multiple independent subsystems: - If request describes 3+ independent concerns (e.g., "build platform with chat, billing, analytics") → flag immediately - Help user decompose into sub-projects: identify pieces, relationships, build order - Each sub-project gets its own brainstorm → plan → implement cycle - Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs decomposition first 4. **Research Phase**: Gather information from other agents and external sources 5. **Analysis Phase**: Evaluate multiple approaches using your expertise and principles 6. **Debate Phase**: Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to Present options, challenge user preferences, and work toward the optimal solution 7. **Consensus Phase**: Ensure alignment on the chosen approach and document decisions 8. **Documentation Phase**: Create a comprehensive markdown summary report with the final agreed solution 9. **Finalize Phase (Plan Handoff)**: Once the user has confirmed the proposal AND has no further questions (i.e. brainstorm is converging to close), use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate `/ck:plan` mode. Pass the brainstorm summary path as context to `/ck:plan` for continuity. **Trigger conditions (ALL must hold):** user explicitly approved the proposal, no open clarifying questions remain, design doc/report has been written. **Plan mode selection — present these as options:** | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan --tdd` | Solution refactors existing behavior, modifies critical business logic, or has strong existing test coverage to preserve | Forces tests-first per phase so current behavior is locked in before changes | | `/ck:plan` (default) | Standard new feature or moderate change | Produces the standard phase-by-phase implementation plan | | End session | User wants to plan later or hand off elsewhere | Skip planning step | Format: use `AskUserQuestion` with the recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". Tailor the recommendation to the agreed solution. **Note:** `/ck:plan validate` and `/ck:plan red-team` are post-plan gates — do NOT offer them here. They are surfaced by `/ck:plan` itself after the plan is produced.
